justifications.durability: The distinction is carried by the type (int | None), by named tests that pin both directions including the payload's fixed key set, and by comments that state the mechanism rather than the incident. Residual risk: no shipped consumer reads the payload, so the contract is held by tests alone, and the comments must stay true of kernel behaviour they cannot test.
justifications.evidence: The run's declared evidence re-checks: 76 passed in the focused suite, whole-tree ruff exit 0, and a control whose declared mutation is byte-identical to the file it was taken from (first-line sha256 equal), whose red run fails at test_throttling.py:658 with assert None == 0 on the root capture, after which the source was restored and the same test re-ran green. I independently re-derived the live root group and the account slice and found the fixture values matched (field set, zeros, force_idle 4197). Deduction: the compute user slice is absent without a session, so that fixture's provenance is supported by a live instance of the same state (login session scopes) and the run's capture, not by a re-read from its original host today.
justifications.fit: The section's question is what an absent period counter and a genuinely zero one mean, and the change answers it where the ambiguity lived: the module no longer decides that a missing cpu.max implies no accounted period, and takes the counters from cpu.stat's own text. The docstring and the CpuStat comment now state the two states and why neither may be reported as the other, which is the section's subject.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The node's goal was to make an unaccounted period tell apart from a measured zero, and it does so at both levels: CpuStat carries int | None per counter and the payload carries 0 for a group that states zeros and null for a group that states none. I reproduced both states from live kernel text with the pre-repair and reviewed revisions side by side; the pre-repair revision reports null on the live root group whose cpu.stat states 0 (the defect, reproduced) and the reviewed revision reports 0. Named tests pin the distinction from both directions, including one asserting the two no-ceiling states are distinguishable from each other and from a quota-ed group.
justifications.scope_discipline: Both commits touch exactly the declared write paths and nothing else: throttling.py and its test in the fix, the plan and the archive evidence section in the docs commit. The figures directory was declared and unused, which is not a violation.

Independent review of run r-20260921T210109150827-fleet-accounting-is-not-the-ceiling (node fleet-accounting-is-not-the-ceiling, plan imas-ambix:slurm-hosted-agent-fleet section 7), read at head ebed4c9f99de01bce684842749c34b3b85500b9f over base e300915f2baab96547b96117dd47c4ad4037919e. Source: 0b2c98d9 (imas_ambix/agent/throttling.py, tests/agent/test_throttling.py) and 7ae35ef2 (docs/plans/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet.html, docs/evidence/archive/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet-landed.html). Both live states were re-derived from the running systems rather than accepted from the fixtures, by loading the pre-repair revision (e300915f) and the reviewed revision side by side and reading /sys/fs/cgroup with each (log: runs/r-20260921T211439392430-review-of-accounting/logs/live-root-group-check.log).

Q(a) Can a caller tell an absent period counter from a genuinely zero one? VERDICT: yes, through the counter values, and NOT through throttled_share. Evidence: on the live root group (no cpu.max; cpu.stat states nr_periods 0, nr_throttled 0, throttled_usec 0) the reviewed revision's payload carries nr_periods 0, nr_throttled 0, throttled_usec 0, permitted_usec null, throttled_share "unbounded"; the pre-repair revision under the same kernel text reports nr_periods null for the same group, which is the defect reproduced from live text rather than from a fixture. For the state that states no counter at all the payload carries null for the three counters. JSON null and 0 are distinct values, every key is present in both cases so the absence is a value rather than a missing key, and CpuStat.nr_periods is typed int | None. The residual, stated because it is the only way the two could still be confused: throttled_share is "unbounded" in BOTH no-ceiling classes, correctly, since neither has a ceiling to take a share of, so a consumer reading only the share sees one value for both states. The distinction lives in nr_periods and throttled_usec (0 vs null), and the module docstring says a caller acts differently on each.

Q(b) Does every fixture that names a provenance carry data from that source? VERDICT: yes for the three that claim a source. Evidence: _QUOTA_ED_MAX ("The account slice on the login node") is "400000 100000" and matches the live cpu.max of the account slice. _CPU_STAT_ROOT_WITHOUT_CEILING (the root capture) matches the live root group read at review time: same field set, the four period counters and nr_bursts/burst_usec at 0, core_sched.force_idle_usec 4197 identical, and a usage_usec that is a plausible earlier reading of the same cumulative counter (8962276463874 against 8971850344764 now, growing forward as a since-boot counter must). _CPU_STAT_WITHOUT_PERIODS (the compute capture) is internally consistent (user 244704 + system 156696 = 401400, against usage 401401, the same +1 tick the live root states) and its shape -- usage/user/system/core_sched only, no period counters -- matches a live instance of that state on the login node's session scopes. The compute host's user-slice directory is absent right now because no session is open there, so that specific capture is not re-derivable from its original host today; a live instance of the same state exists and matches it in shape, and the run's own capture is recorded in the archive evidence section. Fixtures that name no source (_CPU_STAT_TEXT) or declare themselves known-value synthetic (_HOST, _UPTIME_TEXT) make no provenance claim and are not counted. The defect repaired was the reverse case -- a fixture labelled as the compute node whose counters were the quota-ed fixture's with the period lines deleted by hand -- and the replacement carries its own consistent capture.

Q(c) Did the payload shape change, and would a prior-shape consumer break loudly or silently? VERDICT: the key set did not change; one class's values moved from null to 0 within an unchanged shape, so a prior-shape consumer changes behaviour at the value level with no exception -- silently, and in the direction of a truer reading. Evidence: the pre-repair module nulled all three period counters whenever cpu.max was absent; the reviewed revision returns the stated 0 for the root class and null only where the text states none. No key was added or removed, which the payload's fixed-key tests assert, so JSON consumers keep parsing. A repo-wide grep finds no consumer of this module anywhere -- only its own file, its test, and plan/crew state text -- so no in-repo caller exists to break either way. The previous null in that class was the defect being repaired (it discarded a count the kernel kept), so a consumer that branched on None for root-like groups was branching on wrong data; the change moves that branch onto the true 0.

Q(d) Does the module docstring and comment state the two states correctly against the live systems? VERDICT: yes. Evidence: imas_ambix/agent/throttling.py:21-30 now states both -- "A group the cpu controller never attached a ceiling to accounts no period, and a compute node's user slice states none. A group with no ceiling file of its own can still carry accounted periods -- the root group the machine's whole run is accounted under is exactly that -- and those counters are genuine values, zeros included" -- and the CpuStat docstring repeats the distinction for the field level. Against the live systems: the root group /sys/fs/cgroup on 98dci4-srv-1006 has no cpu.max (No such file or directory) and its cpu.stat states nr_periods 0, nr_throttled 0, throttled_usec 0, nr_bursts 0, burst_usec 0, core_sched.force_idle_usec 4197, exactly the first state; the compute node's user slice states no period counter at all, and a live instance of that state is the login node's session scopes, which state only usage/user/system/core_sched. Both sentences are true of the systems they name, and the general claim that a group the controller never attached a ceiling to accounts no period is the one the compute capture and the session scopes support.

Control: the negative control is genuine. The receipt's first line is byte-identical to /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/reports/fleet-accounting-declared-mutation.txt (both sha256 91bb4c1f10eeff919eaa5204e8ffd76ec5f7... on re-check), the red run failed at tests/agent/test_throttling.py:658 with assert None == 0 on the root capture, the source was restored, the same focused test re-ran green, and the worktree diff after restore is the fix itself.

Scope: git show --stat on both commits -- 0b2c98d9 touches imas_ambix/agent/throttling.py and tests/agent/test_throttling.py; 7ae35ef2 touches docs/plans/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet.html and docs/evidence/archive/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet-landed.html. All four are in the run's declared write paths and nothing else changed; docs/figures/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet was declared and unused.

Not verified here, by the discipline of this node's fence: the merged suite at ebed4c9f. Verifying the merged result belongs to a separately dispatched test node; the run's own gate (76 passed, ruff exit 0) is its evidence and was not re-run by this review.
